fluff.overview:
The Grommet is a seventy-five-ton IndustrialMech originally designed as an AgroMech for the agricultural world of Doneval II in the Federated Suns. During the Succession Wars era, the planet's wealthy farming community funded the conversion of these rugged agricultural machines into what would become known as MilitiaMechs, armed combat units built on industrial chassis. Unlike typical field modifications of IndustrialMechs, the Grommet was purpose-designed with a fusion of military-grade and civilian equipment, resulting in a surprisingly capable second-line combat platform.

The design represented the resourcefulness of Doneval II's citizens, who lacked off-planet military support and were forced to develop their own defense capabilities. The Grommet's dual-purpose nature allowed it to continue performing agricultural duties during peacetime while standing ready for planetary defense, making it one of the earliest and most successful examples of the MilitiaMech concept.
fluff.capabilities:
The heart of the Grommet is its fusion reactor, a rarity among IndustrialMechs of the Succession Wars period. This powerplant gives the seventy-five-ton machine a top speed of fifty-four kilometers per hour and provides the energy output necessary to support military-grade weaponry alongside its industrial systems. The design's primary armament consists of a large laser and a class-five autocannon, providing respectable firepower at medium to long ranges, while a vehicle flamer offers close-range antipersonnel capability. The Grommet carries sufficient armor protection to rival lighter heavy BattleMechs such as the Ostroc and the RFL-3C Rifleman, giving its pilots a genuine chance of surviving sustained combat.

The design's agricultural heritage provides unexpected tactical advantages. A grain harvesting combine can be turned to grisly effect against infantry formations, while the right arm-mounted chainsaw serves as a formidable melee weapon against attackers that close to physical combat range. A front-mounted dumper and four-ton cargo bay, originally intended for agricultural work, give the Grommet useful logistical flexibility in the field. Eleven heat sinks manage the thermal load of its weapons systems, though the design's industrial origins mean it lacks the sophisticated electronics and fire control systems found on purpose-built BattleMechs.
fluff.history:
The Grommet originated on Doneval II, a sparsely populated but wealthy agrarian world in the Draconis March of the Federated Suns. Lacking dedicated BattleMech assets or significant off-planet military support, the planet's prosperous farming community took the unusual step of funding the conversion of their heavy AgroMechs into armed combat platforms. The resulting MilitiaMech represented an ambitious project that exceeded the quality typically seen in improvised IndustrialMech conversions, blending military-grade weapons and armor with the rugged industrial systems already in place.

The Grommet received its baptism of fire in September 3039, when the first battalion of the Ryuken-go invaded Doneval II during the War of 3039. The Draconis Combine forces expected an easy victory over what intelligence reports indicated was a lightly defended world. The Doneval Militia had organized itself along decentralized lines, however, making it resistant to the Combine's raiding tactics. Unable to deliver a knockout blow to any single location, the Ryuken-go found themselves drawn into a prolonged campaign against an unexpectedly tenacious foe.

After weeks of skirmishing, the militia mustered its full strength (two battalions of D90 Grommets supported by several vehicle companies) and struck at a Combine-held mining installation. The ensuing battle was fierce and costly. The Grommets suffered devastating casualties against the professional DCMS troops, with few machines surviving the engagement. The handful of surviving Grommets and independent hover vehicle companies refused to surrender, however, conducting guerrilla operations against the occupiers until Armed Forces of the Federated Suns reinforcements arrived in late October to relieve the planet.

The defense of Doneval II, though won at terrible cost, demonstrated that even improvised militia forces built around converted IndustrialMechs could delay and attrite a professional military unit. The Grommet's performance validated the MilitiaMech concept years before it gained broader recognition across the Inner Sphere, proving that a well-designed armed IndustrialMech was far more than a weapon of last resort.
fluff.deployment: This variant is the militarized conversion of the standard Grommet AgroMech, representing the armed configuration fielded by the Doneval II Militia. The conversion retains the base chassis's fusion reactor and industrial frame while adding a large laser and class-five autocannon as primary weapons, supplemented by a vehicle flamer for antipersonnel work. The existing agricultural equipment (including the grain combine, chainsaw, and cargo systems) was retained rather than removed, giving the D90 the unique ability to return to farming duties between conflicts. This dual-purpose approach, combined with heavy industrial armor providing protection comparable to lighter heavy BattleMechs, set the Grommet apart from the crude field modifications that would later proliferate across the Inner Sphere as the MilitiaMech concept gained wider acceptance.
